listing_basis: CITES Appendices in force after CoP20 (Samarkand, 24 Nov - 5 Dec 2025). CoP20 adopted no new timber listings; proposals to remove Central African Afzelia bipindensis and Pterocarpus soyauxii were rejected; the Paubrasilia echinata annotation #10 was amended.
disclaimer: Macroscopic identification is a screening tool, usually reliable only to genus or group. Confirm species with an accredited wood-anatomy, DNA or mass-spectrometry laboratory and the live Species+ listing.

annotations.none: No annotation - ALL parts and derivatives are covered (including finished products).
annotations.#1: All parts and derivatives, except seeds/spores/pollen, seedlings or tissue cultures in vitro, cut flowers of artificially propagated plants (timber, finished goods covered).
annotations.#2: All parts and derivatives except seeds and pollen, and finished products packaged and ready for retail trade.
annotations.#4: All parts and derivatives except seeds, spores and pollen, seedling/tissue cultures, cut flowers of artificially propagated plants and a few plant-specific items (Vanilla, Opuntia etc.). For timber: logs, sawn wood, veneer, plywood, chips AND finished products ARE covered.
annotations.#5: Logs, sawn wood and veneer sheets.
annotations.#6: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets and plywood.
annotations.#7: Logs, wood chips, powder and extracts.
annotations.#10: Amended at CoP20 (2025): in principle ALL parts and derivatives (incl. bows, bow blanks, logs, sawn wood), except finished musical instruments, parts and accessories moved NON-commercially (performance, personal use, exhibition, repair etc.) without change of ownership. Check Species+ for the exact text.
annotations.#11: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood, powder and extracts (finished products containing extracts as ingredients are exempt).
annotations.#12: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood and extracts.
annotations.#14: All parts and derivatives except seeds/pollen, seedling cultures, fruits, leaves, exhausted agarwood powder and finished retail products (agarwood chips, oil, powder ARE covered).
annotations.#15: All parts and derivatives except (a) leaves, flowers, pollen, fruits, seeds; (b) finished products up to 10 kg wood of listed species per shipment; (c) finished musical instruments, parts and accessories; (d) D. cochinchinensis (covered by #4); (e) Dalbergia spp. from Mexico (covered by #6).
annotations.#17: Logs, sawn wood, veneer sheets, plywood and transformed wood (HS 44.09, e.g. decking, flooring strips).

non_timber_listed_trees: Balmea stormiae (App. I, Mexico/Central America - shrubby tree, not a timber)
Tree ferns Cyatheaceae/Dicksoniaceae (App. II - trunks traded as fibre/horticultural)
Palms such as Dypsis decipiens (App. I), and other horticultural trees
Commiphora wightii (guggul resin) and other resin/medicinal trees

taxa.range: Atlantic coastal forest of eastern Brazil (Bahia to Minas Gerais / Espírito Santo).
taxa.heartwood: Dark chocolate-brown to purplish/reddish brown with irregular black streaks (spider-web figure); oily feel.
taxa.odour: Distinct sweet, rose-like scent when freshly cut.

endgrain.deposits: dark red-brown gum in some pores
special: Parenchyma forms fine wavy tangential bands and lozenge-aliform patches around pores

taxa.key_diagnostic: Dark heartwood with black streaks + rose scent + medium pores (few, solitary/short multiples) + banded/aliform parenchyma + very fine rays. Cannot be separated reliably from other Dalbergia (esp. D. spruceana, D. latifolia) by hand lens alone.
taxa.lab_methods: Fluorescence of ethanol extract, DART-TOF mass spectrometry and DNA have been used to separate D. nigra from look-alikes; macroscopic ID = genus level only.

taxa.population_scope: All species except D. nigra (App. I). D. cochinchinensis = #4; Mexican populations = #6.
taxa.range: Pantropical: Central & South America, Africa, Madagascar, South & Southeast Asia (c. 250-300 species).
taxa.heartwood: Very variable: purple-brown, red-orange, chocolate, nearly black; often streaked.
taxa.odour: Many species fragrant (rose, spicy, sweet) when cut or sanded.

endgrain.deposits: red-brown to black gum in some pores
special: Rays and parenchyma storied: ripple marks often visible on tangential face
Fine, regularly spaced parenchyma bands (sometimes wavy) between pores
Rays very fine - barely visible even at 10x

taxa.key_diagnostic: GENUS LEVEL: diffuse-porous, few medium/large pores, fine banded + aliform parenchyma, storied rays (ripple marks), dark often fragrant heartwood. Treat any wood matching this pattern as SUSPECT Dalbergia (CITES App II) until proven otherwise.
lookalikes: Machaerium spp. (pau ferro, Bolivian rosewood - NOT listed)
taxa.lab_methods: DART-TOF mass spectrometry, NIR spectroscopy and DNA barcoding are used to reach species level; macroscopic = genus/group.
